summary: Cycle 2 root-caused and fixed five real defects in the task-owned runner, all committed on the task branch (038ae0e6, ce145cc6, 44ffda8a, plus checkpoint 61027ec5): (1) startIosRecording's stop promise hung forever when the recorder child had already exited — it killed a matrix whose five uniwind live legs had ALL passed; (2) the ORI-RN-005 driver's entry reapOwnedOrphans() kills any server/index.ts listener on the backend port, including the backend this orchestrator launches and passes as options.backend — OCR of the failing screens proved the marker turns were one-shot fetches against the reaped port ('fetch failed: Could not connect to the server'); since the driver is write-prohibited, each phase backend is now hosted by a dedicated owner process importing the REAL server code (createChatServer), whose command line the reap's heuristic does not match, with an OwnedBackendHandle adapter over record/status/command files — smoke-verified serving real completions and real rnr-s05-nonexistent rejections; (3) the validator keyed server records by requestId last-write-wins, letting a later aborted record veto an earlier completed one for the same reused chat id — ids now accumulate outcome/model sets; (4) portListening passed '-iTCP' and ':port' as separate lsof arguments, a form lsof silently rejects — every occupancy check was blind, so an attempt-5 backend grandchild held port 4000 through four attempts EADDRINUSE-ing every phase backend; (5) environment hardening: NODE_OPTIONS dangling --require sanitization (the scratch reaper deleted a cmux shim and every inheriting node child — including biome's linter — died before running), sha256-pinned auto-restore of the Expo Go APK the reaper deleted twice, and phase-root preservation of the driver's web export. Along the way the run also proved: all five uniwind live legs green under orchestration with recording on (disproving the cycle-1 recordVideo-concurrency hypothesis), a nativewind ios live leg green under orchestration, and the standalone driver passing. What remains unmet is the final contract: one fully-green six-target matrix run and the vitest GREEN capture — blocked tonight by a stall INSIDE the ORI-RN-004 (uniwind) driver's live-phase web leg under orchestration (android legs passed at 19:14 UTC, then 45+ minutes with the driver awaiting something async, no maestro/adb/chromium/expo child alive, orchestrator event loop idle; the driver never wrote its live manifest). That driver is outside this task's allowlist. typecheck and the scoped biome command are green on the committed tree; the evidence root was cleared of partial-run output (only the cycle-1 proof.red remains).
assumptions: Run 3's six dead phases were an environment regression (scratch reaper deleted the pinned Expo Go APK), not code — I restored the APK from the official expo/expo-go-releases release as the ORI-RN-005 evidence README documents, and later made that restore automatic and sha256-pinned.

The cycle-1 recordVideo-concurrency hypothesis was tested and disproven: with the passive OCR observer + maestro driver reset, all five uniwind live legs passed with iOS recording running concurrently.

The ORI-RN-005 entry reap killing the caller-passed backend was routed around orchestration-side (owner-process backend hosting the real server code) rather than escalated, because the task's boundary contract expects the orchestrator to pass the owned-backend handle and the fix fit entirely within the allowlisted runner file.

The scratch reaper's deletions (APK x2, cmux NODE_OPTIONS shim, tmpdir web dists) were treated as recurring environmental interference to be defended against in the runner (auto-restore/sanitize/preserve) rather than as a task-contract error.
blockers: The ORI-RN-004 uniwind driver (tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/live-example-proof.test.ts — WRITE-PROHIBITED to this task) stalls indefinitely during its live-phase web leg under this runner's orchestration: after the ios and android legs pass (android/dark screenshot 19:14:06 UTC, run ORI-AI-002-1789929365070), the driver never reaches its web-leg browser/export work (no chromium/expo/adb/maestro children), never writes its live run-manifest, and the orchestrator idles in the event loop for 45+ minutes. Needs the ORI-RN-004 owner to isolate (suspects: web-leg wait on a condition the orchestration's dist/port state never satisfies, or another reaper-deleted prerequisite inside the leg).

Consequently the two runtime verification commands remain unsatisfied this cycle: the exact six-target matrix command has not concluded green, and the vitest GREEN capture (which spawns its own fresh matrix) has not run — no completion can be claimed.

The agent-scratch reaper intermittently deletes runtime prerequisites mid-run (Expo Go APK twice, cmux NODE_OPTIONS shim, tmpdir web dists within one session). The runner now self-heals all three known cases, but any 1.5-2h matrix remains exposed to new reaper targets during its window.

scope_impact.found: The remaining blocker is the ORI-RN-004-owned uniwind driver (tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/live-example-proof.test.ts, write-prohibited to this task) stalling in its live-phase web leg under orchestration (run ORI-AI-002-1789929365070): after the ios and android legs pass, the driver never starts its web-leg browser/export work (no chromium/expo/adb/maestro children alive), never writes its live run-manifest, and the orchestrator idles in the event loop for 45+ minutes.
scope_impact.change: The ORI-RN-004 owner must isolate and fix the web-leg stall before the six-target matrix and vitest GREEN can conclude; once the driver completes its web leg under orchestration, this task's runner (already fixed and committed at 44ffda8a) can execute the full matrix and capture GREEN.
